parsed.answer: Evidence [11603066] shows that phosphotransfer specificity in the CheA(3)/CheY(6) two-component system is governed by a methionine finger on the cognate response regulator, and that introducing this methionine plus an adjacent alanine into noncognate CheYs dramatically changed their specificity while allowing rapid phosphotransfer from CheA(3)-P. Thus the determinant of regulator specificity is also the determinant of rapid phosphotransfer, consistent with a correlation between rapid phosphotransfer rates and histidine kinase regulator specificity. The other two sources concern chromatin/histone phosphorylation and provide no relevant support.
